description_short.value: Small Accra-based maker of cocoa powder, breakfast cereals, food supplements, detergents and laundry starch, listed on the Ghana Alternative Market since 2015.
description_short.source: Written by us from the HORDS PLC financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (GSE PR 140/2026: report of the directors, principal activities; note 1, general information) and GSE PR 275/2015 (IPO results and listing)

description_full.value: HORDS PLC is a Ghanaian-owned company, registered in 1999 to research, develop and produce cereals, detergents and food supplements. It processes local raw materials such as cocoa, cassava, soya and herbs into food supplements, breakfast cereals, detergents, disinfectants and laundry starch. Its brands include Brown Gold natural cocoa powder, Soyabetix, Cocobetix and Spray Starch. It also lists agricultural consultancy and the import and export of goods among its activities. HORDS raised capital in an initial public offer managed by Gold Coast Brokerage, and its shares began trading on the Ghana Alternative Market (GAX) on 11 August 2015. It is a very small business. Production was moved from Kanda to the North Industrial Area in July 2024, and Brown Gold production restarted on 24 December 2024 with 19 staff. In 2026 the company moved its registered office to Adama Abli Street, Nungua, Accra. Its related company is Ghana Growth Fund, a private equity investor that has also lent to it. It reports in Ghana cedis, with a financial year ending 31 December.
description_full.source: Written by us from the HORDS PLC financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (GSE PR 140/2026, a scanned document: general information; report of the directors, principal activities and related companies; note 1, general information), the HORDS PLC 2024 Annual Report (GSE PR 473/2025, chairman's address), the unaudited statements to 30 September 2026 (GSE PR 433/2026, note 14, loans), GSE PR 337/2026 (change of registered address) and GSE PR 275/2015 (IPO results, listing and first day of trading)
